answer_raw:
The fastest option for running an LLM is a **GPU Droplet** using 1-Click Models, which allows you to deploy models like Llama variants directly through a partnership with Hugent Face [8].

The cheapest droplet that would run a 7B model is likely a **v5 configuration** or a **Basic Droplet** with enough RAM to hold the model, as the lowest-cost entry point for virtual machines is **$4/month as of January 2026** [2][5].

## Comparison of options

| Option | Type | Monthly Price | Best Use Case |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **GPU Droplet** | Specialized | Undated | **Fastest performance** for LLM inference [8] |
| **v5 Droplet** | Configurable | Hourly (no monthly cap) [1] | Picking specific CPU/RAM for tasks |
s | **Basic Droplet** | Starts at **$4/month as of January 2026** [2] | Lowest cost development/bursty workloads |

For a 7B model, you typically need at least **8GB to 16GB of RAM** depending on quantization (typically 4-8GB for 4-bit quantized models, as of 2025). Since I didn't find the specific pricing for high-end GPU Droplets or the exact cost of a high-RAM v5 configuration, you should check the DigitalOcean pricing page for the specific resource tiers required to fit a 7B parameter model into memory.
